newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: DROUGHT TIGHTENS GRIP ON AUSTRALIAN STATE OF NSW.
newsitem.headline: DROUGHT TIGHTENS GRIP ON AUSTRALIAN STATE OF NSW.

text.p: The drought-declared area in the Australian state of New South Wales increased by 13 percent to 63 percent in August, Agriculture Minister Richard Amery said on Friday.
This was the largest area of the state which had been drought-declared since October 1995.
"Good general rains are now urgently required to ensure a satisfactory winter crop harvest," Amery said.
"We could be about to enter another period of extended drought and farmers and state governments need to know what commitment the federal government is prepared to make," he said.
Even normally safe winter grazing areas were now drought-affected, having received only patchy effective rain since last summer/autumn, he said.
Severe frosts, preceded by up to six months of low rainfall in some areas, had retarded pasture growth significantly, he said.
This was particularly evident in the southern and central tablelands and highland areas, he said.
The situation in the west of the state continued to deteriorate, with seasonal winds during August and September expected to impact on remaining pastures, he said.
Some areas in the west had been continually drought-declared for a year and a half and in many cases stock owners were selling stock in anticipation of a long dry spell, he said.
Although patchy rainfall received in July and early August had improved crop prospects in the central and southern slopes the crop outlook was now on a knife-edge, he said.
Some areas in the central west, south south west and north west urgently required rain, he said.
With almost four million hectares sown to winter crops, the state now faced average yields rather than a bumper harvest, he said.
